ai.description: *Trachischium monticola* is a small, slender snake reaching 30–40 cm. It is glossy brown or black above with a pale belly and lacks a distinct neck. It is identified by its smooth, iridescent scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trachischium monticola* is best distinguished by its single internasal scale, whereas most similar *Trachischium* species possess a pair of divided internasals.
ai.habitat: *Trachischium monticola* inhabits moist, high-altitude temperate forests and alpine meadows in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 2,000 and 3,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mountain Worm-eating Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through leaf litter and soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trachischium monticola* is oviparous, laying a small clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatching observed in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trachischium monticola* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
